31a8210014d49944.text: Welcome to the platform team at Larkfield. Here's how we used to call models. Four teams, four providers, four keys, and one key sat in a chat screenshot with a lot of thumbs up.

914f5787ebeeef0c.text: Then one Saturday night, Support's provider went down. Priya's assistant stopped answering customers, and we couldn't point it anywhere else, because the provider's name was written into its code.

43119ad575448983.text: A week later a provider renamed one of its models. Three of our apps had the old name typed in by hand, and all three broke before breakfast.

2e767ce636aa9157.text: And every month Jonas in Finance gets one invoice. He asks which team spent it and which provider answered. All we can give him is a shrug.

df5f47b3e0325864.text: My favourite exhibit. A research script retried one failing call all weekend. By Monday it had spent the month's budget, and it was still asking, very politely.

24fbf854b6356430.text: So Tomasz built a gateway, one front door for every model call. A team asks for a plain name like support. The gateway holds the keys, picks the provider and writes down every call.

69012d0f766f9967.text: Three more teams want to move in next month. Before they do, I want someone who has never seen it to tell us what it really does, not what Tomasz's notes say it does.

fe22fd6c65e6cb37.text: That's you. We've built you a small copy with a pretend provider, so there's no real bill. Send it a call, then find out where it went, what it counted, and how it complains.
